aiOverview.content: Forecasters and climate agencies are predicting a potential "super El Niño" in late 2026 following a rapid transition from La Niña. NOAA has issued an El Niño watch, with a 62% chance of development by June–August 2026, which could persist into 2027, triggering record-high global temperatures, significant storm risks, and intense global weather disruptions. This video discusses the potential impacts of the 2026 super El Niño on global weather:39sH24 Hava XəbərləriYouTube • Mar 14, 2026 39s Key details regarding the 2026 Super El Niño forecast include: Timing & Probability: An El Niño watch is in effect, with expectations of developing in early-to-mid summer 2026 and strengthening by fall/winter. There is a roughly 1-in-3 chance of a "strong" or "super" event. Definition: A super El Niño occurs when equatorial Pacific ocean temperatures reach 2∘C2 raised to the composed with power C2∘C or more above average, potentially releasing massive amounts of heat into the atmosphere. Global Impacts: Weather: Increased likelihood of extreme heatwaves, intense flooding, and altered precipitation patterns worldwide. U.S. Impact: Typically brings wetter, cooler conditions to the Southern U.S. and warmer, drier conditions to the North. Hurricanes: The phenomenon could create a hostile environment for Atlantic hurricanes, potentially reducing their activity, but may increase activity in the East and Southwest Pacific. Context: This potential event follows a period of extreme ocean heat, prompting concerns that it could push global temperatures toward new records in 2026–2027. Note: While signs point to a significant event, experts advise that climate models have higher uncertainty in spring and will become more accurate closer to summer.
